findings.outcome: Actual Firebase gateway returns committed registration identity with verificationEmailPending when delivery fails. AccountUseCases binds the real local owner; UI explicitly retries only verification, then consent/navigation. Real Drift owner upgrade and SDK-shaped create/link tests cover repeated delivery failure then success and normal controls. Prior consent recovery and bind-failure compensation retained; no provider signout/deletion used as assumed email compensation.

Exporter receives bootstrap configured base registry including learning preview, and evaluates persisted runtime override/expiry in its existing Drift transaction. Preview/custom/field combinations cover expired/false overrides and active emergencyOff; archive schema, hashes and privacy contract unchanged.

Consent mutation acquires SQLite write lock with a no-op active-owner update and validates unique active intended owner before consent/withdrawal writes. Deferred accept and withdraw after owner A to B switch fail atomically with unchanged owner/consent/secondary snapshots; fresh B action and same-owner lifecycle controls pass. No remote research activity.

conclusions: Registration catches delivery failure only after successful account creation/link, preserves identity and emailVerified=false, then existing AccountUseCases performs owner binding/entry clearing and its prior failure compensation. UI retains session, separates verification retry from consent retry, and never reruns create/link. Tests use real gateway/use cases/Drift upgrade/UI and SDK-shaped fakes; repeated send failure then success, positive controls and F03 consent recovery preserved.

Archive receives configured base registry including preview wrapper. Persisted emergency overrides still evaluated from the same Drift snapshot and UTC expiry. No exported field, manifest, schema or owner/global privacy changes. Four configuration combinations plus exact archive tests.

Consent no-op update takes SQLite writer lock, validates unique active owner, and commits decision/withdrawal work atomically. A switched owner causes rollback before any consent or secondary mutation. Same-owner and synthetic local lifecycle/withdrawal tests preserved.
